title: Save a smaller model, check the files, and run it again
intro: A smaller model file must still load and run. I implemented tools linking weight compression, saved-file checks and execution in a fresh process (Q), and tools that reduce output error after channel removal and restore the smaller structure (R). This work relates to model deployment tooling and save/reload validation. The two experiments use different models and metrics.
qtitle: Q · Save smaller weight files and run them again
rtitle: R · Reduce output error inside a fixed smaller MLP block
try: Run a CPU example of saving and reloading
qmethod: Applied GPTQ quantization with LLM Compressor and compressed-tensors: linear-layer weights become 4-bit integers (INT4) while input activations remain 16-bit floating point (BF16), called W4A16. The final output head is excluded. Checked the saved model files (artifacts), then verified actual vLLM/Marlin execution in a fresh process.
rmethod: Kept the remaining channels fixed in layer 13 of the model’s MLP calculation block, counting from zero. Used calibration inputs to fit its output weights with a CPU FP64 ridge system solved by Cholesky. Saved the corrected output matrix (down projection) as BF16; the loader rebuilds the smaller structure from the saved layer sizes.
qdefinition: Weight-file bytes relative to the BF16 original. This is saved storage, not a reduction in error rate or GPU memory.
memory: Peak memory allocated by PyTorch (allocator), GiB
memoryScope: Allocator peak includes the fixed 1 GiB KV cache and initialization/execution allocations. It is not whole-device peak memory or weight-file size.
scores: The same correct count, different probability scores
qscore: Q-BF16 is the original and Q-W4 the converted model. Both scored 137/192, but one previously correct answer became wrong and one wrong answer became correct. Negative log likelihood (NLL) measures probability assigned to the independently computed correct token; lower is better.
nllScope: Change means candidate minus BF16; negative is better. Differences are paired by question, averaged with equal weight per task, with pointwise 95% intervals. Full-vocabulary and four-choice scores normalize probabilities over different sets, so one improved while the other worsened. On code, both models always chose D, scoring 16/64. Neither gave an allowed answer the highest full-vocabulary score on any of those 64 prompts.
qTiming: Fixed eight-token request, BF16/W4 time ratio:
timeScope: 12 fixed inputs, three process rounds; 95% interval. The interval includes 1, so these measurements do not establish a request-speed advantage.
rnames: I25 removes 25% of one MLP's channels using independent group scores; P25 uses signed pairwise interactions at the same budget. S50 is the shared 50% removal set. The suffix -R means output-weight repair. A group contains 192 adjacent channels; 16 groups form the original 3072-channel MLP.
relativeError: Mean relative output error: before → after
improved: Inputs with lower output error across fixed positions:
rScope: Relative error uses the native MLP output norm at 32 fixed positions per prompt. Energy recovery pools squared errors and is a different metric. Repair changed only down_proj.weight; tensor shapes, parameter counts and the number of inference matrices stayed fixed.
rConclusion: Local reconstruction improved in every held-out prompt, but correct counts moved in different directions. The same-size before/after request-time intervals all include 1. Inputs are short synthetic questions from shared template families; this is not a measure of recovered general model ability.
report: Read the structured report and exact definitions
fixture: A separate tiny randomly initialized model runs through matrix slicing, saving, process exit, directory copy and reload in a fresh CPU process. The example checks structure, complete outputs and shared weights. It does not download a pretrained model or measure answer quality or speed.
routes: Choose a route: inspect recorded results, run the tiny CPU example, build a full model artifact, or reproduce the frozen study.

download: Read / save the displayed source JSON
qJudgment: Implemented: linked existing GPTQ conversion to weight/settings checks, copy verification and execution in fresh vLLM processes.
Reason: file size or conversion success alone cannot establish that saved files are complete, structurally compatible and using the intended execution path.

Evidence: save/reload boundary tests and original runtime records check structure, weights and actual execution. This explains the implementation; it does not claim new comparisons against other designs.
Limit: evidence covers this model and environment. Case009 separately compares longer real requests. File-size reduction does not establish GPU-memory or accuracy improvement.
